Logic and Math pooled: 3,288 questions; only setups that finished both. How to read this page · Method

Latency is the wall time of each request from our machine; runs that shared a GPU or ran with several requests in flight slow each other down, so throughput (questions / min) depends on the run's concurrency. In flight: requests in flight on average, the sum of request latencies over the run's active time (its first to last answer with gaps of more than 10 minutes left out), e.g. “≈ 6” is six at a time.

Median latency is per request; with several requests in flight a run finishes faster than requests × median.

SubQ Snap Preview and SubQ Snap 1.1 returned the same answer to every question (and the same probabilities on 3,276 of 3,288); shown once.

Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) and Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell): two setups of the same model, one on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) and one through Perplexity's API; not verified to be identical weights or settings. Its row is the API setup on every test; Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) is under the row's other settings and All setups.

Not in Logic and Math yet

Logic and Math pools only setups with a complete English run on both benchmarks. 11 setups not yet: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (chat) (missing Logic); Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (on · chat) (missing Math); GPT-6 Luna (max · chat) (missing Logic and Math); Claude Haiku 5.5 (max · chat) (missing Logic and Math); Qwen3.8 Flash (off · chat) (missing Logic and Math); Claude Fable 5.2 (chat) (missing Logic and Math); Grok 4.7 (chat) (missing Logic); Gemini 4 Carbon (chat) (missing Logic and Math); Spark-X2.6-4B (high · chat) (missing Logic and Math); Qwen3.5-4B (on · chat) (missing Logic and Math); Gemini 4 Carbon (high · chat) (missing Logic and Math).

Tie groups and “not measured”

estimate · RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / DGX Spark = run on our own hardware; its cost is an estimate, explained on hover, focus or tap of the amount: the machine's wall-clock time on the run, first to last answer while it was running (pauses, estimated from gaps of more than 10 minutes between answers, left out and listed), × $2.49/h per NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) (Runpod's price for the card) or × $0.213/h per NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) (its purchase over three years plus electricity; see Method), each run charged in full even when runs shared the machine, so at most; sorting and the cost chart use the estimate; list = maker's list price × our token counts; unmarked = provider's price × usage the API reported.

Latency is the wall time of each request from our machine; runs that shared a GPU or ran with several requests in flight slow each other down, so throughput (questions / min) depends on the run's concurrency. In flight: requests in flight on average, the sum of request latencies over the run's active time (its first to last answer with gaps of more than 10 minutes left out), e.g. “≈ 6” is six at a time.

Median latency is per request; with several requests in flight a run finishes faster than requests × median.

Class: by the maker's total parameters, or by list price when the size is undisclosed *

Size by total parameters, as disclosed by the maker (for MoE models the label also shows active parameters): Tiny under 6B · Small 6B–15B · Medium over 15B up to 40B · Large over 40B. Models of undisclosed size, by standard list price per 1M input tokens: Efficient up to $0.50 · Workhorse up to $3 · Flagship over $3. Undisclosed: neither a disclosed size nor a list price.

Not in Logic and Math yet

Logic and Math pools only setups with a complete English run on both benchmarks. 2 setups not yet: Spark-X2.6-4B (high · chat) (missing Logic and Math); Qwen3.5-4B (on · chat) (missing Logic and Math).

Tie groups and “not measured”

estimate · RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / DGX Spark = run on our own hardware; its cost is an estimate, explained on hover, focus or tap of the amount: the machine's wall-clock time on the run, first to last answer while it was running (pauses, estimated from gaps of more than 10 minutes between answers, left out and listed), × $2.49/h per NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) (Runpod's price for the card) or × $0.213/h per NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) (its purchase over three years plus electricity; see Method), each run charged in full even when runs shared the machine, so at most; sorting and the cost chart use the estimate; list = maker's list price × our token counts; unmarked = provider's price × usage the API reported.

Latency is the wall time of each request from our machine; runs that shared a GPU or ran with several requests in flight slow each other down, so throughput (questions / min) depends on the run's concurrency. In flight: requests in flight on average, the sum of request latencies over the run's active time (its first to last answer with gaps of more than 10 minutes left out), e.g. “≈ 6” is six at a time.

Median latency is per request; with several requests in flight a run finishes faster than requests × median.

In flight: requests in flight on average, the sum of request latencies over the run's active time (its first to last answer with gaps of more than 10 minutes left out), e.g. “≈ 6” is six at a time.

Median latency is per request; with several requests in flight a run finishes faster than requests × median.

Class: by the maker's total parameters, or by list price when the size is undisclosed *

Tie groups and “not measured”

estimate · RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / DGX Spark = run on our own hardware; its cost is an estimate, explained on hover, focus or tap of the amount: the machine's wall-clock time on the run, first to last answer while it was running (pauses, estimated from gaps of more than 10 minutes between answers, left out and listed), × $2.49/h per NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) (Runpod's price for the card) or × $0.213/h per NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) (its purchase over three years plus electricity; see Method), each run charged in full even when runs shared the machine, so at most; sorting and the cost chart use the estimate; list = maker's list price × our token counts; unmarked = provider's price × usage the API reported.

Latency is the wall time of each request from our machine; runs that shared a GPU or ran with several requests in flight slow each other down, so throughput (questions / min) depends on the run's concurrency. In flight: requests in flight on average, the sum of request latencies over the run's active time (its first to last answer with gaps of more than 10 minutes left out), e.g. “≈ 6” is six at a time.

Median latency is per request; with several requests in flight a run finishes faster than requests × median.

SubQ Snap Preview and SubQ Snap 1.1 returned the same answer to every question (and the same probabilities on 3,276 of 3,288); shown once.

Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) and Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell): two setups of the same model, one on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) and one through Perplexity's API; not verified to be identical weights or settings. Its row is the API setup on every test; Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) is under the row's other settings and All setups.

estimate · RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / DGX Spark = run on our own hardware; its cost is an estimate, explained on hover, focus or tap of the amount: the machine's wall-clock time on the run, first to last answer while it was running (pauses, estimated from gaps of more than 10 minutes between answers, left out and listed), × $2.49/h per NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) (Runpod's price for the card) or × $0.213/h per NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) (its purchase over three years plus electricity; see Method), each run charged in full even when runs shared the machine, so at most; sorting and the cost chart use the estimate; list = maker's list price × our token counts; unmarked = provider's price × usage the API reported.

estimate · RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / DGX Spark = run on our own hardware; its cost is an estimate, explained on hover, focus or tap of the amount: the machine's wall-clock time on the run, first to last answer while it was running (pauses, estimated from gaps of more than 10 minutes between answers, left out and listed), × $2.49/h per NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) (Runpod's price for the card) or × $0.213/h per NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) (its purchase over three years plus electricity; see Method), each run charged in full even when runs shared the machine, so at most; sorting and the cost chart use the estimate; list = maker's list price × our token counts; unmarked = provider's price × usage the API reported.

Latency is the wall time of each request from our machine; runs that shared a GPU or ran with several requests in flight slow each other down, so throughput (questions / min) depends on the run's concurrency. In flight: requests in flight on average, the sum of request latencies over the run's active time (its first to last answer with gaps of more than 10 minutes left out), e.g. “≈ 6” is six at a time.

Median latency is per request; with several requests in flight a run finishes faster than requests × median.
